channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Spanish Transport Minister Quits in Political Blow for Sánchez
item.description: Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente announced his resignation late on Tuesday, amid growing political pressure after a high-speed train crash killed 69 people.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Data Centers on Midterm Ballots As Opposition Surges
item.description: A Bloomberg analysis shows there will be more than 40 data center-related measures to vote on in the midterm elections. Voters will be considering the proposals as opposition to new data centers surges across the US. Scarlet Fu reports on "Bloomberg Deals." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Deutsche Telekom Said to Hit Brakes on T-Mobile Merger
item.description: Bloomberg's Michelle Davis joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Deutsche Telekom’s plans to combine with its American arm T-Mobile have hit a snag, people familiar with the matter said, casting doubt on what would be the largest-ever public merger. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas, South Carolina Races Could Hinge on Candidate Quality, Says John Thomas
item.description: John Thomas, Republican strategist and managing director of Nestpoint, said that key races in Texas and South Carolina are closer than they otherwise would be as Republicans run embattled or inexperienced candidates in Ken Paxton and Darline Graham. Thomas said he is still 'cautiously optimistic' about the Senate race in Texas, given that Democrats have not been able to win statewide office in decades. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Speed-To-Market Key For Data Centers: Kalka
item.description: Pankaj Sachdeva, senior partner & lead global data center practice at McKinsey & Company, and Melissa Kalka, M&A, private equity partner at Kirkland & Ellis, join Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Midterm voters will be considering proposals as opposition to new data centers surges across the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Court Sides with DOJ in Fight Over Pressuring Election Officials
item.description: A federal appeals court sided with the Trump administration in a fast-moving election fight, lifting a ruling that barred the Justice Department from threatening state and local election officials with prosecution if they count disputed ballots.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman and Greg Stohr

item.title: Apple's Happy Holiday Forecast Overshadowed by Shrinking Margin
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Apple's earnings, which signal strong holiday demand, but show that high memory costs and greater spending on AI will squeeze margins. Plus, Disney plans thousands of layoffs as it aims to cut 20% of costs companywide. And AI is on the ballot in the midterm elections as voters consider local proposals and candidate stances related to AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Midterm Pickups Could Change 2028 Map Says Jim Messina
item.description: Jim Messina, CEO of Fortius Global, said that he is 'cautiously excited' about Democrats' midterm chances, but signaled that he's not taking anything for granted before key races are called. Messina, who served as former President Barack Obama’s 2012 campaign manager, said that if Democrats wins both chambers of Congress, 'the map is much better' for a Democratic presidential candidate looking ahead to the 2028 election. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg News Now
item.description: US Midterm Election Day Democrats Cautiously Optimistic about Results 2026 Most Expensive US Election in History Voters Go to Polls while Gasoline Averages Over $4 per Gallon No Major Moves on Wall Street as Markets Await Election Results Job Numbers Jumped Unexpectedly in September Meta Seeks $15 Billion in USD Portion of Overseas Bonds Trump Claims Netanyahu Agreement in Ending US-Israeli Aide US Strikes Iran's Qeshm Island Crude Oil Moving Lower Zelinskyy & Merz State EU Should Be in Ukraine-Russia War Negotiations (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: America Votes in High-Stakes Midterms
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Election Day is here, with control of Congress and President Trump’s second-term agenda on the line. Oil swings as Tehran signals openness to talks. Wall Street clashes over an AI bubble. Plus, Craig Moffett on Apple’s iPhone Duo, and former SEC Chair Gary Gensler warns a major market repricing could be ahead. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US House, Senate Majority at Stake in Pivotal Vote
item.description: Voting is underway across the United States, in a midterm election that will serve as a referendum on Donald Trump’s second term. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Appeals Court Mulls If Lawmakers Can Sue for ICE Facility Access
item.description: A Washington federal appeals court wrestled with House Democrats’ bid to strike down a Trump administration policy limiting their access to immigration detention centers.
item.dc:creator: Suzanne Monyak

item.title: Gensler Sees Market Repricing Ahead
item.description: Former SEC Chair and MIT Sloan Professor Gary Gensler joined Bloomberg Open Interest to discuss what a change in Congress could mean for financial oversight. He also warns that Washington isn’t moving fast enough on AI risks and predicts a possible repricing of equity and debt markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Election Puts Iran Policy in Focus
item.description: As voters head to the polls, Chicago Council on Global Affairs President and CEO Leslie Vinjamuri discusses what voters’ concerns could mean for Washington. She weighs the prospect of a Democratic House, congressional efforts to influence US support for Israel and whether Congress can constrain President Trump’s decisions on the Iran war. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Whitney Warns of Consumer Strain
item.description: Meredith Whitney, the CEO of the Meredith Whitney Advisory Group joins Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about how the affordability squeeze is still weighing heavily on lower-income households, even as inflation cools. She discusses why higher rates may do little to ease that pressure, how a stagnant housing market and coming layoffs could deepen concerns, and why investors are questioning whether earnings growth can last. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Voting Machines Falter as Westchester Decides Key New York House Race
item.description: Election officials in New York’s Westchester County were racing to address an issue that caused voting machines to reject paper ballots, a snafu that raised the possibility of delays in determining the winner of a key US House race.
item.dc:creator: Laura Nahmias and Cameron Fozi

item.title: Bomb Threats Against Airlines Force Diversions Across Europe
item.description: The European aviation industry was jolted by an unusual spate of bomb threats in the past two days, with planes carrying hundreds of passengers being diverted to airports under the watch of fighter jets. No explosives were found.
item.dc:creator: Kate Duffy

item.title: Trump Says US to Cut $4 Billion in Aid to Israel This Year
item.description: President Donald Trump said he had an agreement with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cut off $4 billion in annual US aid, citing the move as a way to neutralize election-year attacks on Washington’s support for its ally.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: An Election Day Special With Nate Silver
item.description: Nate Silver tells us he is calling this midterms the “rock and a hard place election” — the background conditions are great for Democrats to win both the House and the Senate, but for that to come to pass, the party has to pull off some things that haven't happened in generations, like winning Texas. To believe that will happen requires a certain leap of faith, which is anathema to pollsters. Still, the polls generally believe Democrats are favored, but many professional pollsters would end up with egg on their face if the night does not go that way. Silver — the founder of Silver Bulletin — joins us today to discuss why popular narratives around polling error are wrong, prediction markets, why he doesn't think AI will replace pollsters, and what he is paying attention to tonight as the polls close. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, Iran Pursue Diplomacy Despite Limited American Strikes
item.description: Tehran and Washington are reviewing fresh proposals from mediators on how to resolve their differences and avoid a return to all-out war, according to a diplomat briefed on the matter, after limited US airstrikes overnight.
item.dc:creator: Fiona MacDonald and Ahmed Elimam
